newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 9.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Tuesday told the parliament that she had directed Bangladesh missions abroad to make maximum efforts to attract foreign investment.
Former Bangladesh President A.S. Sayem died in Dhaka on Tuesday.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina will visit Germany from July 13 to attend a UNESCO sponsored seminar in Hamburg.

The ruling Awami League has shunned its earlier plan to form parliamentary standing committees unilaterally and instead asked a senior cabinet minister to discuss the issue with main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP).
Jamaat-e Islami Bangladesh on Tuesday called a countrywide strike on July 15 protesing the circulation of posters by zionists that disgraced prophet Mohammad.
Cargo handling at Chittagong Port resumed on Tuesday after a five-day deadlock as merchant dock workers withdrew their strike.
Two agreements, one on reciprocal protection and promotion of investments and the other on avoidance of double taxation, were singned between Bangladesh and Poland in Warsaw on Tuesday.
The government is considering introduction of "mono-rail" and construction of flyovers in Dhaka city to tackle growing traffic congestion. REUTER
